anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Mis-tuned engine parameters cause internal components such as memory pools, checkpoint frequency, logging, parallelism, or worker counts to operate out of alignment with hardware capacity and workload characteristics.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes saturate host CPU cycles, driving run-queue depth and scheduler waits regardless of the SQL-layer reason for the demand.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : The network path, listener, authentication, or session-slot layer cannot keep pace with attempted client traffic, leading to backlog, retransmissions, or connection exhaustion.

When these three root causes strike concurrently, the system exhibits intertwined symptoms: 1) end-users observe sporadic slow logins, connection time-outs, and sudden query latency spikes; 2) server-side metrics show near-continuous CPU saturation even while some cores idle waiting on client I/O or log flushes; 3) wait-event profiles oscillate between client read/write, socket backlog, spin waits, and log/checkpoint stalls; 4) operating-system socket tables fill and clear in bursts, coinciding with periods of runaway context switches and load-average peaks; 5) post-upgrade or recent parameter changes precipitate flurries of checkpoints and background-writer activity that steal CPU from already strained listener and worker threads, amplifying queueing on both the network and execution layers.

Causal interaction: An ill-chosen configuration (e.g., overly aggressive parallelism, undersized work-memory, tight checkpoint intervals, low connection limits) inflates CPU demand and background activity, pushing the host toward compute saturation. As CPU headroom disappears, listener and authentication threads slow down, prolonging connection setup and increasing socket backlog, which in turn causes clients to retry, compounding network traffic. The surge of half-open sessions and retransmissions further taxes kernel networking stacks and database process scheduling, while misaligned memory and logging parameters trigger additional flushes and context switches that keep CPUs busy but unproductive. The reinforcing loop—misconfiguration driving CPU pressure, which hampers network handling, which then provokes more retries and engine overhead—creates a systemic bottleneck that disrupts both transactional and analytical workloads until configuration is corrected, capacity is added, or traffic is throttled.

entry.official_description: Error, maximum number of retries exceeded when waiting for the internal server session state to be operating
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
